These devices frequently have sensitive data on them. It is, therefore, crucial to guarantee the network is safe and secure because typical security procedures do not apply to Internet of Things (IoT) devices. This research discusses various security algorithms that developed recently and the importance of having well-built datasets with numerous features that simulate real-life situations to verify the proposed models. This paper consists of a comparison between current Machine learning (ML) and Deep learning (DL) algorithms for security systems. In this paper, various MLP models have been envaulted using the CICIDS2017 dataset and we have also proposed a modified version of the KNN classifier in order to improve the existing KNN classifier.

articleTitle: Optimal Machine Learning Model for the Relationship Between Grain Size, Channel Thickness, and Grain Boundary Trap Density in 3D NAND Strings
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: The rapid growth of the semiconductor industry has resulted in the development of three-dimensional NAND (3D NAND) strings, which offer increased memory density and greater performance over classical planar NAND designs. In this work, we look at the critical aspects that determine the performance and reliability of 3D NAND strings. Using simulation results and machine learning algorithms we focus on the effects of grain size, channel thickness, and grain boundary trap density. We address their individual and cumulative effects on memory cell behavior, with the current state-of-the-art strategies used to optimize these characteristics. This work will be helpful in the ongoing development of 3D NAND flash technology.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Based Optimal Operation of Distribution Systems Integrated with Electric Vehicles Using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: This paper proposes a data-driven based optimal operation of distribution systems integrated with electric vehicles (EV) using Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). Historical data on EV charging patterns and loads are employed to train the DNN, which is then tested on distribution systems. It is observed that the used DNN architecture accurately predicts the voltage magnitudes and angles, which can be used for calculating the remaining optimal power flow (OPF) parameters. This process reduces the computational burden substantially and demonstrates adaptability for varying EV penetration levels and load patterns, making it a scalable and flexible solution for smart grid implementations. The proposed model is implemented and validated on the IEEE-33 bus distribution system.

articleTitle: Model Order Reduction Using Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: This paper works on a new method i.e., Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm (AOA) for reducing the higher order linear time invariant (LTI) complex system to reduced order system by retaining their original state of the system. Here we have used Routh Array Criterion for reducing the denominator and AOA used for reducing the numerator. The analysis of parameters was conducted to examine the dynamic behavior of a system and identify any improvements in Integral Square Error (ISE), when compared with additional previous techniques, current method's Integral Square Error is slightly lower.

articleTitle: Functional Safety Assessment of Battery Management System of Autonomous Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: There has been an exponential increase in the usage of electric vehicles in recent years. Electric vehicles are powered by batteries for all their functions. Battery management system (BMS) helps to manage the inherent risks associated with batteries and their associated systems. Functional safety assessment of BMS plays a key role in identifying all the failure causes, associated risks and suggesting improvements in design. In this work, a comprehensive assessment of functional safety of the BMS of autonomous electric vehicle is carried out based on ISO 26262. Hazard Analysis and Risk Assessment (HARA) is used to determine the hazards and their risks. Quantitative Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) is carried out for identifying all the possible causes of failure and determine its probability of failure. Since the preliminary system architecture was not satisfying the threshold failure rate of violation of safety goal defined in the standard, some safety measures are integrated into the system. FTA is repeated for the modified system. The modified BMS meets the target failure rate as per ISO 26262, ensuring the functional safety.

articleTitle: Tracing Food Products in Supply Chain Using DLT Enabled Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: The most emerging new technology of trust is the concept of blockchain technology, which is a combined ecosystem of entwined dependencies of agricultural supply chain and agricultural produce. A sufficiently high transparency is the most essential requirement where agricultural produce and supply chain are to be implemented in a combined manner. Thus, blockchain is emerging as the most reliable and secure way to ensure consumer benefits. The ledger of records, usually maintained in the form of blocks, are encapsulated and maintained in a network. The newer records are stored in the next block and each of the existing block is connected to the newer block so that the sequence of blocks in maintained. Each block leads to the next block in the chain and the distributed nature of the network ensures transparency and integrity of each block. Any alteration in any block by any agent can be easily detected and the integrity can be maintained. Cryptography is another major concept that plays a pivot role in ensuring security and integrity of the blocks formed. Various types of online transactions, documentations, or records can be managed using blockchain technology. In particular, agriculture is a sector which fulfils the demand supply chain of food and the demand for better quality food is having the highest demand.

articleTitle: IoT Based Plantation System for Smart Home Farming
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Home smart farming is the area where Internet of things (IoT) applications are expanding. The effectiveness and quality of agricultural goods have been recommended to be increased by using various monitoring, controlling, and tracking systems. Many people would like to start their own small-scale farms at home to produce organic goods for their daily consumption, even if the majority of the existing systems concentrate on industrial farming. However, due to a lack of agricultural infrastructure and understanding, people are frequently unable to produce healthy agricultural goods and are also unable to safeguard their indoor plants from too much and too little sunshine. The IoT-based plantation system described in this research attempts to maximize plant growth while shielding plants from excessive or insufficient sunlight. The system uses sensors to assess important environmental variables such as light intensity, and temperature, integrating IoT technology with agriculture. The gathered data is processed, examined, and sent to a cloud server for archival and examination. Real-time data visualization, notifications, and user interaction are made possible through a user-friendly mobile application. The main focus is on protecting plants by keeping an eye on light levels to prevent harmful consequences of excessive or insufficient sunshine exposure. The system uses the IoT infrastructure to assure ideal circumstances for plant growth as well as remote monitoring and control, which results in effective resource management.

articleTitle: Temperature Independent Resistorless CMOS Voltage Reference
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: This paper present a method for generation of low supply voltage temperature independent voltage reference circuit using only MOSFET. This reference voltage is generated by the diode connected MOSFET. This voltage reference circuit has combination of Complementary to absolute temperature (CTAT) and Proportional to absolute temperature (PTAT) along with two stage Operational Amplifier (Op-Amp) to get high gain. The proposed design is simulated in Cadence-Virtuoso using TSMC 180nm technology. Designed circuit achieves a temperature coefficient of 62.31 ppm/° Celsius while line regulation is 0.3386 % and reference voltage variation is 0.508 %. Temperature changes from (0-100)° Celsius. Area occupied by proposed design is 3.058nm2 and Power consumption is 4.1489 mW at 27° Celsius.

articleTitle: Sentimental Voice Recognition: An Approach to Analyse the Emotion by Voice
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Emotion analysis is essential for efficiently interacting with people and understanding their situations. Emotion recognition assists us in locating or comprehending a person's emotional state, which is critical in emerging computational technologies. Nowadays, people interact with computers textually, while other people interact with computers in video form, or display-based scenarios, where people can get their current sentimental state and the computer provides them with analytical results by using a different algorithm to get that person's current emotional state with the help of previously provided data. Speech provides a wealth of information, such as information about a person's goal, desire, and internal state. The feelings and reactions of a person are distinct in that they reveal the person's mood, intention, and purpose. In proposed work, we practically add the voice of different people with different moods and hence we are able to get the desired result, the result shows the person's emotional state like happy, sad, angry, etc.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Risk Factors for Appropriate Screening of Cervical Cancer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Cervical cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer as well as death from cancer in women worldwide. Effective screening programs especially in low-income countries are the need of the hour. Using Machine Learning methods, we can analyze the risk factors associated with cervical cancer. In this report, we present a comparative analysis of 4 Machine Learning Algorithms, Support Vector Machine(SVM), Random Forest Classifier(RFC), K Nearest Neighbour(KNN), and XG-Boost(XGB) in classifying various cervical cancer screening techniques, namely, Hinselmann, Schiller, Cytology and Biopsy based on the associated risk factors. Instead of using classification accuracy which is less relevant in imbalanced medical datasets, we evaluate the models based on ROC-AUC scores and Precision-Recall AUC scores. Finally, we extract the relevant features by calculating feature importance using permutation importance. The results obtained are consistent with the medical science research.

articleTitle: Novel Adaptive Threshold Algorithm for Through the Wall Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive threshold algorithm for the through-the-wall imaging data. The traditional algorithm works well in fixed and predictable backgrounds separation from the foreground. The need for an adaptive threshold algorithm arises due to complex practical scenarios, especially in military instrumentation. Researchers have proposed many algorithms for unknown background separation, but challenges remain to separate the wall reflections and undesired targets giving false alarms. The proposed algorithm uses a combination of image data variance and normal random variable variance. Experiments have been conducted to show that the proposed algorithm offers satisfactory results.

articleTitle: Melanoma Detection Using Channel and Block Attention Module
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Early Melanoma detection is a challenging task due to an imbalanced dataset and less number of labeled images. There are many methods based on different Deep CNN architectures however as the interclass similarity is very low, more focus on the target area is highly required. In this paper, a dual Attention module is proposed at the skip connection part of ResNet101 after the convolution block. The proposed model used a channel attention module to increase the weight of the channel that contains more relevant information. The model also used a spatial attention module to highlight local features in the spatial domain. Proposed model score classification accuracy 95.1%, sensitivity 87.6%, and specificity 95.8%. The proposed model achieves better classification accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity than other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Enhancing Plant Leaf Disease Classification Performance Through EfficientNetB3 and Hyperparameter Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Plant diseases pose a significant risk to global food supply and finances. This research paper develops a system using EfficientNet-B3 to classify plant leaf diseases. The PlantVillage dataset, with 54,303 curated images, is utilized. The model accurately identifies plant leaf diseases, with extensive testing and comparisons. A user-friendly web platform allows convenient submission and classification of plant leaf photos, providing prompt and reliable results for disease identification. The research has implications for revolutionizing plant disease detection and control strategies. By utilizing deep learning and EfficientNet-B3, this system offers an effective method for early disease detection, enhancing agricultural practices, and improving global food security.

articleTitle: Development of Image Analysis Based Methodology to Detect Weed in Drone Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Weed infestation is a major problem faced in precision agriculture, and detecting infested area in a large field for its elimination is itself a very tedious task. Detecting weed patches via aerial images using digital image processing techniques is not much explored and relied-on method especially in the cases of overlapping color channels values of target and background and involvement of complex feature detection techniques, since normal feature detection methods do not provide clear outputs in such cases. In this paper, we have explored to develop an image processing-based methodology to detect weed with aerial image (UAV image) and we found quite encouraging results. This will also help in reducing the computational complexity.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Programmed Face Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: This study proposes a unique method for a programmed face monitoring system that makes use of a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller and Mediapipe, a well-known computer vision framework. The system makes use of Mediapipe's real-time face detection technology and a PID controller algorithm to precisely monitor the identified face by dynamically adjusting the pan and tilt angles of a servo motor system. The usefulness of the proposed approach is demonstrated by the graphical representation depicting setting time, steady-state error and the oscillation type. The results were compared between Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID), Proportional-Derivative (PD) and Proportional (P) controllers. The PID controller showed favorable results among all three of the controllers utilized in the face monitoring system. For PID controller-based faced monitoring system, the setting time of the system designed is obtained as 1 second, the steady-state error is low and the oscillation type observed is critically damped. The usage of this method for programmed face monitoring systems has a potential application in a number of fields, including robotics, human-computer interaction, and surveillance systems.

articleTitle: A Compact Substrate Integrated Waveguide-Based Multiband Antenna with Seamless Integration for UAV-Based Agricultural Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have revolutionized agriculture by enabling remote monitoring, data collection, and precision farming. To ensure reliable wireless communication between UAVs and ground-based systems, compact multiband antennas with seamless integration are crucial. This paper introduces a Compact Substrate Integrated Waveguide based Multiband Antenna (CSMA) designed for UAV based agricultural applications. The CSMA operates across multiple frequency bands, including 5.85 GHz, 7.9 GHz, and 9.8 GHz for crop growth monitoring, soil moisture monitoring, and pest monitoring. The compact size and lightweight design by utilizing Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) enable integration onto UAV platforms without compromising flight performance. The cavity backed SIW structure allows unified integration without causing any interference from the ground plane of the antenna. The CSMA comprises a ring-shaped slot along with two parasitic rectangular slots for achieving the multiband response. An extra shorting via is also positioned inside the SIW cavity to reduce the radiation nulls. Thus, unidirectional and stable broadside radiation is achieved with a realized gain of 6.65 dBi, 5.0 dBi, and 5.3 dBi at 5.85 GHz, 7.9 GHz, and 9.8 GHz, respectively with overall radiation efficiency greater than 94%. The antenna design addresses wireless communication needs in agricultural settings, using UAV platforms.

articleTitle: Hybrid Minkowski Fractal FSS Based Multiband Polarization Insensitive Radar Absorber
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: It is still a difficult issue for researchers to achieve optimal absorption at the same time, polarization insensitivity, in the development of microwave absorbing structures. In this paper, a unit cell influenced by hybrid fractal geometry is created in such manner that absorption at six resonance frequencies occurs in C, X, and Ku bands. The designed structure exhibits an excellent absorption incidence angle up to 90° for transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) mode. The simulation results show a peak absorptivity greater than 95% at 4.1 GHz, 7.1 GHz, 9.5 GHz, 11.7 GHz, 14.0 GHz and 17.5 GHz, respectively. The surface current distributions are plotted, which support the absorption phenomena at resonant frequencies.

articleTitle: Development of Methodology for Multiple Low Dielectric Targets Detection Using TWI Radar System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: In through wall imaging (TWI) radar system, the detection of multiple target having dielectric contrast behind the wall is a quite challenging task. This adds on to the confinement in cases where targets have been put in excessively noisy environment. In this proposed work, a methodology for the detection of multiple low dielectric targets in the presence of high dielectric one is developed and explored. An experimental data is collected for the detection of target. The B-scan images for different scenarios is taken and analyzed using the image dynamics adjustment technique. A satisfactory agreement with the findings of detection is established as per the scenario using the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Multi-Mode Tunable Terahertz Microstrip Patch Antenna For Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: A terahertz (THz) microstrip patch antenna is proposed to achieve the tunability of the antenna performances through controlling the external biasing. The antenna comprises of the single layer of graphene placed on the top of the patch. This graphene is biased to tune the chemical potential over the range of µc=0.5-0.9 eV. This tunability is reflectable from the reflection coefficient and gain behavior. The antenna operates over the frequency range of 1–7 THz with best gain of 7.73. This proposed antenna with tunable feature aid in building up the more robust and flexible communication devices.

articleTitle: Novel Design of Metamaterial Inspired Substrate for Compact Dual Band Stacked Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: A novel approach for designing Metamaterial (MTM) based substrates for Stacked Microstrip Patch Antenna (SMPA) has been analyzed with an aim to design most compact antenna ever resonating at dual band frequencies in L5 and S band. The reported antenna has a miniaturized electric size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50\ \text{mm}^{\ast}\ 50\ \text{mm}^{\ast}9.69\ \text{mm}(0.196\lambda 0 \times 0.196 \lambda 0\times 0.038 \lambda 0)$</tex> making it suitable for compact antenna to be used in IoT devices and/or as Global Navigational Satellite system (GNSS) receivers. The cross polar discrimination (XPD) value of 16 dB and 12 dB at L5 & S band respectively provide reliable circular polarization (CP) operation with global bandwidth of 30 MHz at both frequency bands. The design of SMPA over traditional substrate, over Reactive Impedance Surface (RIS) substrate and over substrate with MTM inclusion have been compared in term of radiation performance and in context to antenna size for targeted frequency bands.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of FIR Filter Using Quaternary Base Number System (QBNS)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: This paper proposes an FPGA implementation of a Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter using a Quaternary base number system (QBNS) multiplier. QBNS FIR filter is a well-organized and powerful filter that can be widely used in various applications, such as audio and video processing, wireless communication, biomedical signal processing, control systems, and various DSP applications. Quaternary base number system (QBNS) is totally a new concept that uses 4 bases 2,3,5,7. This paper presents simulation results for a Quaternary base number system FIR filter on Xilinx FPGA. Our research shows that using the Quaternary base number system multiplier results are more accurate compared to the Double base and Triple base number systems.

Author Keywords: Single Term Quaternary Base Number Systems(SQBNS)

articleTitle: Q-Learning Based Network Access Policy Management for Zero Trust Security in IIoT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Network protection is a major concern with current technology development. Zero trust security is an emerging trend irrespective of the domain and application area. Zero trust security is a model that ensures authentic access to the network. In recent years, zero trust security has attained notable significance in research and real-world practices to accomplish the security desires of the technologies. To overcome the risk and consequences of cyber-attacks, the application of zero trust security is a novel approach. Various past pieces of research were made targeting on the application and advantages of zero trust security but are not aware of the major challenge in the efficient implementation of the technology. The time consumption of each node authentication and verification hinders the seamless working of zero trust. Integrating artificial intelligence with zero trust is an underlying approach to providing a solution to the time-delay issue. The paper focuses on implementing zero-trust security with artificial intelligence for reducing network access time. The artificial intelligence-enabled zero trust model reported that the network access time is reduced by 18% as compared to CRH-SRP and 38% as compared to Cyber Security via Determinisms

articleTitle: Multi-Factor Behavioral Real Time Authentication for Enhanced Security in Digital Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: This study presents a novel method of authentication in digital environment in which each element of authentication is linked to one another. Having multiple factors to authenticate and deriving co-relations among these increases the safety and security of the device. Types of behavioral and acoustic patterns which are to be considered are GPS, accelerometer, microphone & speaker fingerprint, lip & tongue movement sensing and pinna shape sensing. Pattern data from different sensors is compared and cross checked. Having multiple factors to authenticate and deriving co-relations among these increases the security of device. The main advantage of multi factor behavioral authentication is that the verification is done dynamically and continuously to provide real time security. All authentication activities are carried out in the background without the user being interrupted. Furthermore, because these authentication approaches do not involve the user, the user experience is enhanced along with the security of the device.

articleTitle: sMRI Classification of Alzheimer's Disease Using Genetic Algorithm and Multi-Instance Learning (GA+MIL)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Text, Image, Audio and Video are the data formats used for storing information in today's digital world. In particular, Image processing plays a crucial part in the medical profession for diagnosis of diseases and severity identification, and the modality of input can be either 2D or 3D images. A type of disease named Alzheimer's disease (AD) occurs due to damage to nerve cells (neurons) in the human's brain. Alzheimer's disease is regarded as one of the main causes of death worldwide. Alzheimer's disease diagnosis is a complex task, and no preventive measures have been ascertained yet. This study aims to create a system that uses 3D structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) as an input for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease. Unlike existing architecture like basic Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), the methodology Genetic Algorithm + Multi-Instance Learning (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{GA} +\text{MIL}$</tex>) is an advanced model that works on two levels, Local Feature Extraction and Global Feature Extraction is used for this research. In general, the partition of Region of Interests (ROI) from sMRI images is basically divided into three categories namely, 1) Voxel (volumetric pixel)-level, 2) Region-level and 3) Patch-level methods. Correlation and overfitting problem is a major drawback in Voxel-level method whereas Region-level method has the disadvantage of not including all the disease related features. To overcome this problem, the Patch-level method of partition of ROIs is adopted in this study. Hence the initial sMRI is preprocessed, then divided into patches and passed into the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{GA} +\text{MIL}$</tex> model. The experimental results show that the usage of Genetic Algorithm to identify discriminative pathological locations results in efficient global feature extraction.

articleTitle: Hybrid Cloud Service Portability Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: The software industry is heading towards cloud solutions which give them better scalability, security, and availability all at the same time. The companies deploy their important assets to various cloud platforms which offer the required solutions. Many times these requirements change according to the industry's demand-supply chain and hence companies try to migrate between different cloud platforms taking those same assets, but they face many difficulties with data security and sanctity as there are hardly any flexible ways of transfer. We desire to create a ‘Hybrid Cloud Service Portability Platform’ which would offer a seamless migration between cloud solutions overcoming the impediments like vendor lock-in, uncountable hours of transfer and security checks, bad mobility, etc. We try to build a zone that helps relocation from ‘any cloud to any cloud’ with minimal time and effort and irrespective of the size of the data. This project has the potential to add a new perspective to hybrid cloud technology and solve many concerned problems. Currently, the scope of the solution is limited to migrating a Load Balancer from AWS to GCP. We have explicitly defined AWS as the source cloud platform and GCP as the target cloud platform.

articleTitle: Camouflage Target Detection Using Deep Learning with Drone Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: In the task of camouflaged target detection, the target is highly integrated with the background textures, which makes it difficult to detect and leads to false detection or missed detection. A detection algorithm YOLOv5s has been used for the detection of camouflaged targets to explore the detection effect of using Artificial Intelligence on camouflaged targets. On the other hand, the use of drones for object detection as well as camouflage detection increases in many fields like military, civil, agriculture, etc. detection of hidden objects using drones and UAVs need to explore with efficient Deep Learning (DL) models. Drone data was used in this study to identify bounding boxes for military-like camouflage targets. This paper helps to fine-tune YOLO v5 and evaluate performance results. It is validated on the dataset obtained from the drone, and the experimental results show that the YOLOv5s can be well applied for detection of camouflaged target detection.

articleTitle: Towards High Efficiency CZTS Solar Cell with HTL Using SCAPS-1D
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: In this study, numerical simulations on designs based on window layer, buffer layer, absorber layer and hole transport layer were conducted with the objective to enhance the performance of a solar cell based on CZTS, to reduce excessive series resistance over the absorber layer and determine the highest conversion efficiency. To examine the optimum power conversion efficiency, ZnS and ZnMgO serves as a hybrid buffer layer, ZnO acts as a window layer, CZTS as an active layer and MoS2 serves as a hole transport layer. We have calculated all the performance parameters of the solar cell based on variations in the capture cross section of electrons/holes at an absorber layer (CZTS) and variations in thickness of hole transport layer (MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). The ZnO:AI/ZnS/ZnMgO/CZTS/MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> photovoltaic cell has highest performance at 32.15% conversion efficiency.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Fire Fighting Hexacopter Drone
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: This paper aims to develop a hexacopter which is designed to carry dry CO2 balls to extinguish fire without risking lives of firefighters with the help of remote-control system. The Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) market is exploded in recent years. The UAV are widely utilized for civil, military, and commercial applications because of ease of deployment, hovering capability, and excellent mobility. UAVs can easily reach heights that are risky and tough for firefighters. This study provides a simple solution of a remote-controlled aerial vehicle which can extinguish the fire. Furthermore, we propose a framework for constructing a drone that is equipped with easily-obtainable components with proper dropping, can be remotely operated and deliver lightweight items to several destinations in one trip. This framework can be applied to emergency scenarios, such as fire-fighting, or to other remote areas, providing an affordable long-term solution with easy component replacement.

articleTitle: Planar Dualband SIW Antenna for K Band and mm wave Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: In this communication, an Antenna with technology named Substrate Integrated Waveguide, loaded with modified bowtie shaped slot using microstrip wave port is designed and simulated. The basic rectangular cavity is achieved in accordance with technology called substrate integrated waveguide technology, it includes copper filled vias between ground plane and top layer of cavity. The overall structure with feeding component is incorporated in the same plane and optimized using software ANSYS HFSS. SIW and modified bowtie shaped resonator are included to improve gain, efficiency and also bandwidth of the proposed structure. The proposed structure uses substrate material as RT Duroid with εr = 2.2 of dimension 30×25×0.508 mm. The structure has two resonance frequencies i.e. 21 GHz and 23.7 GHz with peak gain value 8.06 dBi and 10.07 dBi respectively including efficiency of 90.1 % and 92.2 % respectively. The designed is suitable for K band applications (mm wave radar applications) and also for 5G mid band. The proposed antenna electrical size is 0.37 11×0.31 11×0.0064λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>.

articleTitle: Critical Analysis of Image Processing Based Classical Approach for Camouflaged Target Detection: Computer Vision Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Camouflage is a type of adaptive coloring in which the target blend into its environment making it harder for the predators to see it. It can be accomplished by color matching, disruptive patterns or a combination of the two. Detecting camouflaged targets by naked eyes can be a difficult task or quite impossible as the target foreground and the background have undistinguished patterns and colors. So, a Computer Vision technique is required to examine the content of the images and also a technique that is able to distinguish foreground with the background. This paper aims to provide a comparative study on Camouflaged Object Detection (COD) using various classical computer vision approaches which includes Thresholding, Color Space Model and Image Fusion techniques. The comparative and experimental analysis provides an insight of the classical approaches which can be further used for the computer vision applications.

articleTitle: Direction of Arrival Estimation of Wideband Sources: Trend Analysis of Mean Square Error vs Regularization Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: The goal of this paper is to optimize the Direction of arrival (DoA) estimation of wideband sources based on sparse linear arrays by analyzing the variations of the mean square error of DoAs with respect to regularization parameters. The wideband source signals are partitioned into segments, a Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) is performed, and then data is collected for each frequency bin. To combine the data which is collected from more than a single frequency bins, the Jacobi-Anger approximation is used, which converts the different co-array matrices into a single virtual uniform linear array. There are a number of estimation techniques available with different assumptions to be considered. The work in this paper is focused on a particular practical scenario where the power spectrum of all wideband sources is identical and known in advance. Thus, the DoA estimation approach used in this paper is a super-resolution off-the-grid approach. As the minimization problem is dependent on a factor called the regularization parameter, the dependency of the mean square error on the regularization parameter is analyzed. Simulation results show that the mean square error as a function of the regularization parameter possesses a minimum value only for a certain value of the regularization parameter. Therefore, the selection of the optimal value of the regularization parameter, which is very important, can be done by following the recommended range or value of the regularization parameter rather than using a hit-and-trial method.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband and High – Gain Stacked Cylindrical DRA for WLAN, Wi-Fi, and WiMAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: In this study, a wideband, high-gain stacked cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA) is examined. The antenna consists of two unequal cylindrical dielectric resonators (DRs) with varying permittivity values (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}1}=15$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}2}=2.2$</tex>) that are centrally supplied in order to provide a broad frequency band with high gain. The stacked uneven cylindrical DRA has a diameter of 50 by 50 and is intended for use with WLAN, Wi-Fi, and WiMAX. A simulated bandwidth and peak gain of 4.86 GHz to 6.41 GHz and 9.19 dB are observed by the stacked cylindrical DRA. The software ANSYS HFSS does the simulation. This research paper's antenna design will therefore be useful for wireless applications.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Real-Time Simulator to Evaluate the Power System Stabilizer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: This article proposes a power system stabilizer (PSS) based on Real-time Simulator software for a single-machine infinite bus (SMIB) system. The proposed PSS gives better results than conventional power system stabilizers (CPSS) because the software is better equipped to handle non-linearities and can work accurately and minimize computational time. It can provide more precise control over the power system, which is important for maintaining stability which is examined by the Heffron-Phillips model. The CPSSs are designed to respond to specific types of disturbances, while the Simulator can respond to a wider range of disturbances and provide more precise control proceedings. A Real-time Simulator setup is used to simulate complex systems in real-time.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a 2-D ConvNet for Early and Multiple Target Detection and Binary Classification in Sugarcane Fields Using UAV Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: 2D ConvNets are deep convolution-based networks used exclusively for image modality-based computer vision operations. Used widely in image segmentation, object detection, image localization and classification, 2D ConvNets exhibit promising scope in camouflage target localization and detection. In this paper, we have explored LeNet-5 based 2D CNN to detect multiple weed patches of varying sizes using UAV images and successfully classifying them into two classes, viz weed and non-weed.

articleTitle: Solar Tracker with Obstacle Detection Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to develop a system that combines solar tracking technology with obstacle detection. This improves the safety and energy efficiency of a solar-powered vehicle. Solar powered vehicles face several challenges such as limited range and the need for efficient energy harvesting. This is done by adjusting the solar panel position based on the location of the sun to maximize energy harvesting. This ensures that the vehicle can operate for longer distances and remain charged. The system is designed to be reliable and efficient, and it was able to perform well in various testing environments.

articleTitle: Crop Phenology Studies Using RGB Drone Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: The drone is used in precession agriculture for spraying pesticides, phenology study, and crop classification. Crop phenology is an essential aspect of agricultural resource management and the classification of various crops. Any automated model should be able to identify or classify phenology stages solely on the statistical feature's assessment rather than the visual inspection. The crop has different colors during the growth stages; therefore, the color-based model is attempted for phenology studies with the help of drone RGB images. Rice, soybean, sugarcane, and wheat crops are selected for the phenology study. Various color-based features are used for phenology studies, and it is found that a* band of la*b color space model and 2*G-R-B (Ex-green) bands can classify the crop growth and harvesting stage. The ripening stage can be identified using the R-B band combination. Therefore, these three features combination can be used to identify different growth stages such as stem-elongation, ripening, harvested, and non-harvested stage.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Sensor Based Automated Smart Parking System for Large Parking Space Optimized with a Streamlined Vehicle Allocation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: This research paper presents the development and implementation of a sensor-based automated smart parking system aimed at optimizing parking slot allocation, resource utilization, and payment processes. The system incorporates a low-cost weight load sensor technology for accurate monitoring of parking slot occupancy. The proposed vehicle allocation algorithm (VAA) ensures efficient and precise allocation of parking slots with minimal computational power. Additionally, the system features a fully digital payment system, eliminating the need for physical transactions and enhancing convenience for users. Through the integration of these advanced technologies, the automated smart parking system offers cost-effective and efficient parking management solutions, significantly improving the overall user experience and resource utilization.

articleTitle: An Approach for Validation of Soil Moisture Algorithms in Heterogenous Agricultural Regions Using Synthetic Dataset
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: An accurate estimation of soil moisture (SM) is crucial for management of water resources, drought assessment, hydrology, and crop yield. The dynamics of near-surface SM can be effectively captured using L-band active and passive (AP) microwave (MW) observations. While current global SM information is available through passive L-band missions like NASA's Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) and ESA's Soil Moisture and Ocean Salinity (SMOS), their spatial resolutions of 36 km and 25 km, respectively, are too coarse to provide precise SM estimates in heterogeneous agricultural regions. To address this limitation, this study focuses on developing a synthetic dataset to validate SM scaling algorithms and explore the synergies between AP MW observations at different spatial scales. By employing this synthetic AP MW dataset, the effectiveness of soil moisture algorithms in agricultural regions will be assessed.

articleTitle: Dual-Wideband DGS Based Dielectric Resonator Antenna for C-and Ku-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: A dual-wideband dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is reported with a microstrip feed and two circular cut and rectangular cut horizontally in ground structure as Defected Ground structure(DGS). Radiated electric fields, gain and impedance matching have discussed at the resonant frequencies at 7.2 GHz, 17.7 GHz. At <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7.2\ \text{GHz},\ \mathrm{S}11=-51.19\ \text{dB}$</tex> and at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$17.7\ \text{GHz},\ \mathrm{S}11=-23.51\text{dB}$</tex> demonstrating strong impedance matching at those working frequencies. Overall size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$35\times 35\times 1.575\ \text{mm}$</tex> is provided by the proposed double-band antenna. Additionally, the proposed antenna offers the first band (5.67-8.24GHz), second band (15.58GHz-19.04GHz), have bandwidths of 35.69% and 19.54%, respectively. Maximum Gain 4.4dB at 7.2GHz and 7.2dB at 17.7GHz. Radiation efficiency is seen to be greater than 96% within the targeted operating frequency band 5.67 GHz to 8.24 GHz, and 99% at frequency 15.58GHz to 19.04GHz Proposed antenna is ideally suited for millimetre wave applications in C- and Ku-band suitable for radar and satellite communication.

articleTitle: Frequency Selective Surface-Based Rasorber with Broadband Tunable Transmission Window for Airborne Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: In recent years, frequency selective rasorbers (FSRs) have attracted researchers for low-RCS antenna applications. However, existing passive devices have fixed performance once fabricated and exhibit narrow transmission bandwidth, which are not suitable for reconfigurable and wideband applications. In this paper, a frequency selective rasorber (FSR) with a reconfigurable and wide tunable transmission window in-between two absorption bands is presented. Unlike conventional tunable FSRs, where lossy and lossless FSS screens are loaded with varactor diodes to provide tunable transmission frequencies, the proposed FSR is composed of a single FSS layer loaded with varactor diodes to provide tunable transmission bands. This configuration avoids the requirement of additional varactor diodes, thus, averting undesirable complexity associated with having more lumped components. The proposed FSR has been evaluated by extensive full-wave simulations. The result shows that the passband of the proposed rasorber can be tuned from 8.75-11.89 GHz by changing the reverse electrostatic bias from 0–10 V, with an insertion loss of less than 1 dB. In addition, a wide low-reflectivity band with a fractional bandwidth of 77.9% is realized under the normal incidence. This tunable FSR is expected to find broadband airborne and stealth applications.

articleTitle: Analysis and Comparison of a High-$K$ Dielectric Vertical Channel Based Organic Thin Film Transistor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: In this paper, a vertical channel organic thin film transistor (OTFT) is studied. The device is validated using Silvaco Atlas device simulator. Afterwards, device optimization is performed on the basis of materials and thickness variations. For the optimization, the materials of organic semiconductor and insulator are considered as C8-BTBT and pC1B5, correspondingly. Here, pC1B5 is a high-K dielectric (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{k}=7.5$</tex>) material, which played major role to enhance the device performance. Addition to this, thickness of the different layers is also reduced up to 10nm to make the device more flexible. Moreover, the optimized device is compared with two other existing devices in terms of drain current, saturation mobility, threshold voltage and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{on}/I_{off}$</tex>. The optimized device exhibits significant performance as the drain current and saturation mobility are obtained as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$129.7\ \mu \mathrm{A}$</tex> and 15.5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/V.s, respectively. The drain current of the optimized device (D2) is 1.5 times and 10 times higher in comparison with D3 and D4, respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Modifications of Rotor Flux Barrier in Synchronous Reluctance Motor for E-Bike
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Electric bicycles have become progressively popular due to their environmentally friendly and cost-effective nature. However, choosing a suitable motor is very much needed to attain better performance and energy efficiency. This research paper explores the design and modification of rotor flux barrier in synchronous reluctance motor (SynRM) for an electric bicycle by comparing its Hyperbolic-curve and Hyperbolic-polyline rotor designs. The aim of this study is to determine which design produces more efficiency in terms of power consumption and performance. Both designs were analyzed using finite element analysis, and their performance was evaluated through simulations by Ansys rmxprt. The results revealed that the hyperbolic-curve design had a higher efficiency and better performance compared to the hyperbolic-polyline design. This suggests that the hyperbolic-curve design is a better choice for electric bicycles.

articleTitle: Optimizing RF Parameters in Novel Si1-xGex/GaAs JLTFET Through Ge Mole Fraction Variation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: In this paper, the influence of the Germanium mole (x) on the RF parameters of the novel Sh-<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>/GaAs junctionless TFET (JLTFET) is examined for the first time. In the developed device, a smaller band energy gap Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> is considered at the source, and a larger band energy gap GaAs is incorporated at the drain and channel based on the energy gap technique. The reciprocity of ION, gm, transconductance generation factor (TGF), parasitic capacitances (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gs</inf>, C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gd</inf>, C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gg</inf>), f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>, GBWP, and transit time (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex>) on the Ge mole composition are investigated using 2-D Silvaco TCAD Simulator. The simulated outcomes indicate that the proposed device delivers its best output at Germanium mole fraction <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{x}=0.8$</tex> in the Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> material.

articleTitle: Design of Differential Evolution Optimization Fused Transmission Line Modelling Derived Multilayer mmWave Absorber
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: The design of an absorber specifically for mmWave is very complicated due to the involvement of multiple design variables. Therefore, a cost-effective, efficient, lightweight, wideband multilayer mmWave absorber (MWA) is proposed in this article. MWA is designed and optimized using differential evolution optimization (DEO) fused with a transmission line model (TLM). DEO is used to find out the dielectric properties of the required material along with the respective thickness of each layer for the MWA. The study is carried out for the recently introduced fifth generation (5G) mmWave band in India for single, double, and triple-layer absorbers with reduced thickness. The designed triple layer MWA with a thickness of 1.18mm exhibits compelling results, a reflection coefficient (RC) of −52dB at 26.5GHz with 100% bandwidth (BW) for the entire band below the −10dB threshold. The result shows an excellent match with analytical and full-wave simulations. Considering wideband and lightweight characteristics, the designed MWA is suitable for various mmWave applications.

articleTitle: Design and Investigation of Frequency Selective Surface Loaded Thermoplastic Polyurethane Polymer-Based 5G Absorber
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: In the past few years, numerous efforts have been undertaken towards the development of microwave absorbers that are simple, broadband, angularly stable, lightweight, conformal, and unaffected by polarization effects. This work comprises a single-layer decagonal ring-shaped frequency selective surface (FSS) loaded thermoplastic polyurethane polymer-based absorber for the mm-wave band. The designed absorber with a dielectric substrate having a thickness of only 1.7 mm achieves a −10 dB reflection coefficient (RC) bandwidth of 5.5 GHz (23-28.5 GHz) for the normal angle of incidence. Furthermore, the proposed absorber shows a minimum RC of −28 dB at 26 GHz centre or resonant frequency. Moreover, the surface current distributions at a resonant frequency of the proposed microwave absorber are also investigated. The presented absorber is lightweight, flexible, polarization insensitive, angularly stable, and suitable for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Hardware-Based Implementation of Target Tracking in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have gained sig-nificant attention in various fields, including surveillance, search and rescue, and monitoring applications. One important application for UAV s is target tracking, which requires detecting and tracking a specific object of interest in real time. This paper surveys work done so far in the area of target-tracking in UAV s. It then presents a comprehensive hardware-based framework for target tracking in UAV s. This work utilizes the State-of-the-Art YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once) algorithm for target detection, an efficient high-speed target tracking model, and a Proportional Derivative (PD) control algorithm for precise drone movement control. YOLOv8 provides fast, accurate, and real-time detection of the object of interest, allowing the UAV to detect and identify the target object quickly and reliably. Subsequently, a robust tracking algorithm tracks the identified object across consecutive frames, ensuring accurate localization and trajectory estimation. Furthermore, a PD control algorithm is integrated into the system to enable precise and smooth drone movement. The proposed framework is integrated and used for target tracking in UAV s. Further, this framework is implemented on a UAV. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework, showcasing its potential for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Microstrip Patch Antenna with Optimum Parameters for S band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Circularly polarized antennas are widely utilized in today's wireless communication system due to their resistance to multipath distortion and polarization loss. With the increasing demand for satellite communication, the need for broadening the S band of satellite frequency in the communication sector has expanded, and the usage of S band has become more common. The proposed antenna design features a circular patch and a circular slot in ground plane. Due to its simplicity and ease of application, the defects in the ground are employed to create circular polarization and this technique is known as Defected Ground Structure (DGS) technique. The slotting technique of a microstrip antenna has benefits such as reduced profile, ease of manufacture, ease of feeding, ease of integration into the system, and, most importantly, increased gain. In this work, a microstrip patch antenna with a circular patch radiating element and a microstrip line feeding mechanism is proposed. Design and analysis of circular patch antenna has been done by using CST Microwave Studio Software. The antenna's dimensions are 25mm×25mm×1.6mm. The antenna is made of 1.6mm thick FR-4 lossy substrate, which has dielectric constant 4.3. The 3-dB axial ratio (AR) Bandwidth and Impedance Bandwidth (IBW) of the proposed antenna is 39.66 % and 4.72 % at operating frequency at 2.53 GHz respectively. The proposed antenna has S11 (return loss) of -36.27 dB and -22.51 dB at 2.53 GHz and 4.31 GHz respectively. The maximum realized gain in the boresight direction and voltage standing wave ratio is 3.50 dB and 1.03 respectively, is achieved at operating frequency.

articleTitle: IL-YOLOv5(Improved Loss in YOLOv5): An Improved Multi-Object Detection Model Focusing on Snowy Weather Conditions in Mixed Driving Environments for Self-Driving Cars
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: This paper presents a modified YOLOv5 algorithm named IL-YOLOv5 (i.e., YOLOv5 with Improved Loss) for object detection specifically in challenging weather conditions, specifically focusing on snowy weather conditions in autonomous vehicles. Object detection is a critical component of autonomous vehicle technology, but it can be challenging in adverse weather conditions due to limited visibility and changes in object appearance. The proposed modified YOLOv5 algorithm includes the modified loss function i.e. Focal-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> EIoU Loss instead of CIoU Loss. The algorithm is evaluated on a dataset of snowy road scenes, and the results show a significant improvement in object detection performance compared to the native YOLOv5 algorithm. The bounding box regression process in the model is sped up and the loss is decreased by the IL-YOLOv5 algorithm. Test results showed that the YOLOv5 algorithm is outperformed by the IL-YOLOv5 method based on convergence speed, mAP enhancement by 4.1, and detection speed by a factor of 3.

articleTitle: An Approach to Model Soil and Vegetation with HFSS for Synthetic SAR Data Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data is a powerful tool in vegetation studies, providing valuable insights into the dynamics of vegetation in a changing environment. However, real-world SAR data acquisition is expensive, time-consuming, and limited, hindering the development of robust machine learning (ML) models for various applications. To enhance the accuracy of ML models, there is a need for generating synthetic data. Therefore, this study focuses on electromagnetic modeling of soil and vegetation to generate synthetic backscatter coefficients at L band using the High-Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS). We have created different models for various scenarios with varying incident angles, frequencies, and polarizations, enabling us to explore wide range of SAR imaging conditions. The accuracy of the simulated backscattering coefficients is validated by comparing with ALOS2 PALSAR 2 satellite data and observed a very good agreement between the simulated and observed data.

articleTitle: Design of $2\times 2$ Super-Wideband MIMO Antenna for S/C/X/Ku/K/Ka Band Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel four element super-wide-band multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna. The proposed antenna design displays polarization diversity and radiates over wide range of frequency spectrum. Horizontal and vertically polarized patch radiators are spatially positioned in a perpendicular manner which contributes in achieving reduced mutual coupling and improved isolation greater than 20 dB with a highest value of 77 dB between adjacent and diagonal ports. Circular geometries are etched off from the bottom (ground) plane leading to an improved bandwidth. Parasitic structures in the form of circular hoops on the upper layer and Jerusalem cross on the bottom (ground) plane are added further improving the reflection coefficient(S11) parameters. The novel MIMO structure is based on FR4-epoxy substrate with dimensions 1.03 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda^{\ast} 1.03 \lambda^{\ast} 0.014\ \lambda$</tex>. The novel antenna thus radiates at frequencies 4.45GHz, 5.61GHz, 8.49GHz, 11.37GHz, 12.52GHz, 15.40GHz, 16.55GHz, 18.28GHz and 29.81GHz. The proposed novel design exhibits a super-wideband of 31.82 GHz and can be used for multiple wireless applications. Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) value for the proposed design is less than 0.06 which shows good MIMO antenna performance.

articleTitle: A Decentralised Model for Pricing of Competitive Electric Vehicle Charging Stations Considering the Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: The growing number of electric vehicles (EVs) has led to an increasing number of privately owned EV charging stations (EVCSs). They will engage in competition to maximise their revenues. Also, the prices offered at these EVCSs will influence the charging demands, affecting the operation of the distribution system (DS). This work presents a pricing model for the EVCSs considering their competitive interactions and the DS. The interactions between the EVCSs to maximise their profit is formulated as an equilibrium problem (EP) in the upper level, while the DS market clearing problem is in the lower level. These subproblems are solved in a decentralised way between the EVCSs and the DS by exchanging the charging demand data only. The proposed pricing model is studied for a 15-bus DS with two EVCSs and compared with three different model types to verify its effectiveness in achieving higher profits for them.

articleTitle: A Study to Investigate the Influence of $\gamma$ Radiation on Microwave Absorption Characteristics of Barium Titanate/Exfoliated Graphite Nanocomposite
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Gamma radiation has the potential to induce changes in the properties of materials, affecting aspects like their morphology and conductivity, which in turn influence their microwave absorption properties. The utilization of absorbing materials is crucial in mitigating the impact of electromagnetic (EM) pollution. Nonetheless, achieving a high level of absorption, a broad bandwidth, and maintaining a thin coating thickness remains a formidable challenge. This study introduces an innovative approach to create an ultra-thin, wideband microwave absorber using a γ-irradiated nanocomposite of barium titanate and exfoliated graphite (BT/EG 10 kGy). To achieve this, BT is synthesized through a straightforward and scalable solid-state method, with the addition of 1 wt% EG. Subsequently, the composite undergoes γ-radiation exposure at a dose of 10 kGy. We conducted measurements of the complex permittivity and permeability of the BT/EG 10 kGy sample in 2 - 18 GHz range. The study also explores the impact of grain size and EM parameters on the microwave absorption characteristics due to γ-irradiation. Remarkably, the BT/EG 10 kGy sample exhibits an impressive absorption bandwidth of 10 GHz, spanning from 6.6 to 16.6 GHz. What makes this achievement particularly noteworthy is the ultra-thin thickness of 1.5 mm. The combination of this wide absorption bandwidth, minimal coating thickness, and the straightforward fabrication process employed in this study positions the BT/EG 10 kGy sample as a highly promising candidate for efficient MAM.

articleTitle: Identifier-Based Rendezvous Scheme for Asynchronous Cognitive Radio Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: To achieve blind rendezvous in cognitive radio networks (CRNs), channel hopping (CH)-based techniques are typically used in the literature. In this paper, an identifier-based channel hopping (I-CH) algorithm is proposed to establish blind rendezvous between two secondary users (SUs). The basic idea is to generate CH sequences for SUs with distinct hop patterns and shortest periods based on their respective Identifiers (IDs). The suggested CH algorithm guarantees an optimum degree of rendezvous and reduced maximum time to rendezvous. Furthermore, it is useful for preserving the memory of tiny wireless devices and sensors that are appropriate for device-to-device communication and Internet of Things applications. The effectiveness of the suggested scheme has been assessed with the use of theoretical analysis and simulation findings.

articleTitle: IOT Based Intelligent Bus Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Nowadays, keeping secure while travelling is of utmost importance and in order to prevent unnecessary issues, we must regularly monitor bus performance. There are a number approaches available to monitor buses, but the issue is that it is unable to do it continuously. The continuous monitoring of the bus represents a big problem for the Bus Management system. The bus management system has a number of issues, including the inability to determine whether the driver is intoxicated or whether the bus continues to travel at a normal speed etc. The development of the Internet of Things (IoT) has offered a promising opportunity to address the issues brought on by rising transportation issues. This paper makes use of the components such a microcontroller, a piezoelectric sensor, a speed sensor, an alcohol sensor, a fuel level measurement device, a level switch, GPS, a key, an LCD display, an alarm, a voice board, and an Internet of Things (IoT). If any accident occurs piezoelectric sensor detects mechanical vibration and the location of bus is shared to the bus management system via GPS. A piezoelectric sensor is a machine that is used to detect the mechanical vibration and it electrical signal via the piezoelectric effect. The vehicle's speed is measured using a speed sensor. Alcohol sensors are used to determine whether the driver is consuming alcohol. The fuel level measurement is used to determine the fuel level. The foot step switch is employed to the step for those people who stand on the foot board for an extended period of time and comments are indicated by voice board. The circuit is turned on and off using the key, and the alarm sounds when the bus is travelling too fast. Using an LCD display, the bus parameters are tracked. GPS is used to track the bus. All components are integrated with the microcontroller. Finally, with the use of IoT, Bus management can continuously monitor the performance of the bus in this paper.

articleTitle: Hybrid CNN & Random Forest Model for Effective Potato Leaf Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Potato leaf diseases threaten food production and security. Effective illness prevention and management require an accurate and quick diagnosis. This research proposes a new potato leaf disease identification method using CNN and RF models. Our study uses images of healthy potato leaves and leaves with multiple illnesses, such as Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans), Early Blight (Alternaria solani), Potato Virus Y (PVY), Blackleg (Pectobacterium and Dickeya species), Early Dying (Verticillium wilt, caused by Verticillium spp.), the Fusarium Dry Rot, and Bacterial Ring Rot (Clavibacter michiganensis subsp. sepedonicus). A CNN model extracts significant features from input photos for disease categorization. To predict, we pass the collected features to a random-forest classifier. Our illness diagnosis system is more accurate and robust since we use CNN and RF together. Precision, recall, F1-score, support, and accuracy are used to evaluate our technique. Precision values range from 74.51% to 81.97%, recall values from 70.00% to 80.60%, and F1 scores from 73.04% to 80.00%. Our model has 89.26% accuracy. Our results imply that CNN and RF models can diagnose potato leaf disease. The suggested method correctly identifies sick potato leaves across classes with good precision and recall. The findings help pave the way for more efficient and precise automated diagnostic methods for potato diseases, which will ultimately help farmers and other stakeholders better manage and prevent illness.

articleTitle: Ferrous Metal Segregation with IOT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Recycling of metals has become one of the most important concerns in the modern industrial development. The availability of the rare earth metals keeps on decreasing and the cost of mining increases as we go to higher depth of the planet. Not all metals can be recycled but majority of them can be used till they reach their recyclable cycle limits. Till then they can be used for construction and designing purposes. Metals can be separated by various aspects. The major one is separating metals with their magnetic property. Ferrous metals and non-Ferrous metals. Ferrous metals or alloys or those which have iron in their compounds so that they get attracted to magnetic field. Nonferrous are those which are not attracted to magnetic lines of force but still exhibit some characteristics when they are brought close to magnetic fields. With this property in the metals, they can be separated as magnetic and non-magnetic metals. This is done in metal and alloy industries where, while recycling is done this is one the efficient methods to separate metals having different properties.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Assisted Diagnosis of Speech Disorders: A Review of Dysarthric Speech
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Speech disorders are commonly associated with neurodegenerative impairments in the motor system of the brain. Challenges to speech and communication are often experienced by those with conditions including Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), Cerebral Palsy (CP), and Parkinson's Disease (PD). This review focuses on the machine learning applications for diagnosing speech disorders, with a particular emphasis on dysarthric speech. ALS, in particular, presents difficulties in speech production, spinal functions, respiration, and swallowing, making early diagnosis crucial for improving the patient's quality of life. Sustained vowel phonation emerges as a promising technique for distinguishing among ALS, PD, CP, and individuals in good health. This comprehensive review explores the various machine learning approaches utilized for diagnosing ALS, PD, and CP through speech analysis, highlighting their potential impact on future research.

articleTitle: Development of an Ensemble Machine Learning-Based Decision Support System for Patient Admission in Healthcare Unit
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: This paper introduces a decision support system designed to enhance patient care in healthcare settings. The system employs various decision-making tools, including alerts for emergencies and recommendations for treatment plans, medications, discharge, or transfer to different units, all based on patient data, and medical history. The system achieves an accuracy of 99% by integrating both knowledge-driven and model-driven approaches, seamlessly incorporating user input such as patient demographics and vital signs, along with real-time data on ICU and general ward bed availability. The output is displayed on a user-friendly website that provides suggestions for immediate action in emergencies based on predefined rules. The experiment involves comparing the performance of several classification algorithms, such as decision tree, logistic regression, support vector machine, naive Bayes and with their ensembles. The results indicate that the ensemble models provide the best outcome. The study highlights the importance of accurate decision-making in healthcare and the need for a reliable decision support system. The study concludes with a future scope for extending the system's capabilities, incorporating additional patient data, and further evaluating the system's effectiveness in real-world healthcare settings. Overall, the proposed system is a well-designed machine learning model that can make quick and accurate decisions based on a patient's vital signs.

articleTitle: Investigation of Machine Learning Approaches for Retrieval of Soil Moisture Using NavIC Signal
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC) is India's own navigation system to cater the navigational and surveying need of the Indian subcontinent. The navigation signals transmitted by the NavIC satellites are available round the clock and scientists have found its use beyond the navigation and surveying purposes. The study of soil moisture with navigation signal is one of the most recent applications which has attracted the research community. The ground-based receiver collects the multipath signal, which includes the direct signal and reflected signal from the soil surface, to calculate the multipath phase, which is sensitive to soil moisture. To determine the soil moisture with multipath phase, this work investigates the application of machine learning (ML) technique. The investigation has utilized the support vector machine (SVM), decision tree, random forest (RF), and linear regression techniques. When predicting soil moisture, random forest performs better than other algorithms.

articleTitle: Identification of Rice Leaf Diseases Using CNN and Transfer Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Rice is a crucial crop for global food security, but its production is often threatened by diseases that can significantly reduce crop yields. Detecting and diagnosing these diseases early on is crucial for managing rice crops effectively. The detection and classification of rice leaf diseases can now be automated due to the progress made in deep learning and computer vision technologies. The present study introduces an novel methodology for the identification and categorization of rice leaf ailments utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs), specifically the ResNet50 and VGG16 models. The proposed methodology employs deep learning methodologies to autonomously acquire features from images of rice leaves, thereby enabling the classification of various disease types. The proposed methodology is assessed through experimental trials on a dataset of rice leaf images that encompasses various disease categories. The findings indicate that the suggested methodology attains elevated precision in identifying and categorizing diverse varieties of rice leaf ailments. The ResNet50 framework surpasses the VGG16 framework in accuracy and sensitivity. The method under consideration exhibits the potential to serve as a proficient instrument for disease management in rice cultivation. It furnishes prompt and precise information regarding the disease status of rice crops, thereby empowering farmers to undertake essential measures to curb the spread of diseases and avert yield losses. Furthermore, the suggested methodology has the potential to be applied to various other crops, thereby facilitating the creation of disease detection and classification techniques that are more widely applicable and expandable.

articleTitle: Visual Techniques for Clustering Tendency Assessment of Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Electronics, Communication and Computers (ELEXCOM)
abstract: Graph datasets are gaining popularity in various applications. Analyzing graph data using data clustering could help reveal underlying patterns and understand them better. However, most popular graph clustering algorithms require an estimate of the number of clusters or some other metadata to obtain information about the community structure, a difficult ask for novel datasets.
